newsitem.title: USA: Biogen jumps on strong MS drug sales, Q3.
newsitem.headline: Biogen jumps on strong MS drug sales, Q3.

text.p: Shares in Biogen Inc jumped on Thursday after the biotechnology company posted strong third quarter sales of its newly launched multiple sclerosis drug and better-than-expected third quarter profits.

Sales of the multiple sclerosis drug Avonex, which Biogen began selling in May, topped $27 million in the quarter, Biogen said. "Avonex sales were at the high end of expectations," said Bear Stearns analyst David Molowa.
Molowa reiterated his buy rating on the stock, setting a $110 price target for year-end 1997.
Biogen was up 1-3/4 to 78-3/4 in morning trading.

The company reported third quarter earnings of $1.21 a share, up from $0.03 a year ago. Analysts said the earnings were above consensus expectations, even when taking in consideration a one-time $30 million royalty payment and a one-time $23 million tax benefit in this year's third quarter.

The bottom line was also boosted by expense controls and strong royalty revenues from hepatitis B vaccine, sold by SmithKline Beecham Plc and Merck and Co Inc, and the anti-viral/anti-cancer agent alpha interferon, sold by Schering-Plough Corp, analysts said.

"Not only were the Avonex numbers very strong but the royalty stream is growing again," Oppenheimer and Co's Matthew Geller said. He reiterated his outperform rating on the stock and set an end-1997 price target of $96 on the stock.
Molowa said he raised his 1996 earnings estimate on Biogen to $1.21 a share from $0.96, maintaining his 1997 view at $3.15.
